identity.confidence: XVAL across three sources for the 5.0; the MG is assumed identical from APK analysis and one MG capture [HW]. The 5.0 and MG share a custom-service UUID and are indistinguishable at scan time, so both resolve here. After connect, the Device Information model string tells them apart: an MG unit reports model 'MG' (hardware 'WS50_r03', firmware 50.38.1.0 on the one captured unit). Legacy registry rows stored the bare string WHOOP, and unknown strings default to this family; see docs/protocol/whoop.md.

standard_gatt.confidence: XVAL. The standard heart-rate profile gives live HR and RR with no custom-service handshake; on the 5.0 it needs the phone's OS bond (the whole custom service demands authenticated pairing), unlike the 4.0 where 2A37 answers unbonded.

commands.name: get_hello
commands.note: 0x91. First write of the enable handshake; the gen5 hello is its own opcode, unlike the gen4 hello at 0x23.

commands.name: set_clock
commands.note: 0x0a. Clock sync. b3 unconfirmed on gen5.

commands.name: toggle_realtime_hr
commands.note: 0x03. Starts the standard heart-rate profile; the deep biometric data still comes from the sync buffer, not a live stream. b3 unconfirmed.

commands.name: set_config
commands.note: 0x78. Carries one feature flag per write; see enable_sequence.

commands.name: feature_flag_query
commands.note: 0x75. Begins the feature-flag exchange the app runs before set_config. b3 unconfirmed.

commands.name: feature_flag_next
commands.note: 0x76. Iterates the feature-flag exchange. b3 unconfirmed.

commands.name: get_battery_level
commands.note: 0x1a. On gen5 the response is a direct percent byte, unlike gen4's deci-percent u16. b3 unconfirmed.

commands.name: send_historical
commands.note: 0x16. Starts the historical/biometric offload; records replay as packet type 0x2f, and on the gen5 straps this buffer is the only route to the sensor because there is no live optical stream.

commands.name: historical_ack
commands.note: 0x17. Echo the 8-byte cursor from the status frame back verbatim or the offload stalls after one chunk. Advances the read pointer; deletes nothing. HISTORY_COMPLETE arrives as metadata (type 49) command 3.

commands.name: force_trim
commands.note: 0x19 = FORCE_TRIM. Irreversibly deletes the buffer up to the write head. Never send until HISTORY_COMPLETE has arrived and at least one record came back; b3 is unconfirmed on gen5, hence 0.

enable_sequence.confidence: JUDES for the flag names and format, from an HCI capture round-tripped byte for byte over 8031 frames on a real MG. The official app sends fifteen writes; ten flag names are captured here, five are not yet identified. Each value byte is taken as 1 (enable); the per-flag values were not enumerated in the source, so treat the values as CODE-INFERRED. The name sits ASCII in a 32-byte field, the value byte follows at offset 32 in a 40-byte payload. IMPORTANT [FIELD]: on a real worn MG these flags are accepted and ACKed byte-for-byte but do NOT activate the deep (R22 / type 51-56) stream. Five worn sessions up to 4.1h after a full ACK produced zero deep frames, only plain type-40 heart rate. The deep buffer appears subscription- or server-gated, not BLE-flag-gated, so sending this sequence does not by itself unlock deep data on a no-subscription strap. Carry the sequence because the flags are real and correct, but expect standard heart rate and the ordinary sync buffer, not the R22 firehose, until the true gate is found.

time.confidence: XVAL for the fields (HR cross-checked against GATT 2A37 to under half a bpm), [WRS] for the payload-relative byte positions: layout offsets are into the inner record (payload[0] = packet type), where the timestamp sits at 2 and HR at 8 on BOTH generations — the earlier +4 gen4/gen5 split was an artifact of counting from the full frame (whose header is 4 bytes on gen4 and 8 on gen5). The subseconds unit is CODE-INFERRED and unresolved against GET_CLOCK's 1/32768 units; see the ledger.

confidence_note: Realtime, command subset, and the admitted historical records. Packet 47 (historical_data, inner type 0x2f) is the biometric offload; the layout version rides inner byte [1] (the sequence position), not [2] (which carries the on-wrist r22 command). r20_k18 decodes the full per-second metrics record (HR body[11], R-R count body[12]/values body[13.., gravity three f32 from body[34], skin temp body[62:64] as a raw u16 register gated to 5-45 C, steps body[46], activity class body[52], packed sleep state body[70], the sleep-only tri-mode SpO2 percent body[71] gated to 70..=100, and signal quality body[29]); r20_k26 decodes the 24 i16 raw-PPG burst at body[16:64]. Both decoders are admitted in the core's mav-codec and backed by real 5.0/MG capture goldens (fixtures/records/r20_k18_v1.json and r20_k26_v1.json), imported from tanarchytan/whoop-rs [WRS]. The deep buffers are now decoded too: gen5_v21 emits 100-sample 6-axis IMU (accel body[17]/[217]/[417], gyro body[629]/[829]/[1029]) gated on both sample counts == 100, and gen5_v20 emits the 6-channel x 25-sample 20-bit optical buffer (channels at body[36]/[236]/[1302]/[1502]/[1724]/[1924]) gated on the 2x-green-LED anchor. Both are [PROV]/UNVERIFIED synthetic-only (no real fill captured) and add the stream kinds imu, gyro, optical_raw under ADR-015; the earlier K=18 additions (spo2_percent, activity_class) are ADR-014. The empirical signal_flags bitfield (body[22]) is still recorded but unemitted. Events (packet 48) decode through the admitted whoop vocabulary [WRS]: the number is the inner command byte [2], the RTC unix sits at inner 4, the battery event emits battery_soc (deci-percent at inner 13, / 10, gated 0..=100) and wrist on/off (9/10) emits wrist_state 1/0; other numbers are state transitions with no sample stream. The on-wrist live r22 push is the same K=18 record streamed in real time (command byte 0x80/0x82 marks on-wrist; it is not a decoder selector — replayed sync-buffer records carry 0x80 too), so live and historical share the one version-keyed path. Every fact here derives from docs/protocol/whoop.md and carries that ledger's tags; nothing is hardware-verified by this project yet.
